draft.title: The move from youth to adulthood
card: The move from youth to adulthood is a time of change in roles. Young people often gain more independence and take on more responsibility for their own choices.
Common changes include finishing school, starting study or paid work, moving out of the family home and forming long-term relationships.
These changes can affect health. Paid work can bring income and a sense of purpose, but it can also bring stress, long hours or less time for sleep and exercise.
The effect depends on the person and their situation. Support from family, friends and the community can help a person manage the change.
draft.remember: Becoming an adult brings new roles and responsibilities, and these can help or harm health.

a.q: Which statement best describes how the move to adulthood can affect health?
opts: New roles can help or harm health, depending on the person
New roles harm health, because adults have more stress
New roles help health, because adults have more income
New roles have no effect, because health is set in youth
a.why: The card says new roles can bring benefits such as income and risks such as stress. The effect depends on the person and their support. The option that says adulthood only harms health ignores the benefits.
a.clue: Think about whether the effect is the same for everyone.

b.q: Priya, 19, has moved out of home in Geelong to start a full-time job. She now cooks for herself and pays her own rent. She has little time for sleep or exercise. Which statement best explains her situation?
opts: Independence brings new duties that can affect her health
Moving out of home stops her development in other areas
Paid work always lowers health, as it cuts sleep and exercise
Her health is now fixed, because she has become an adult
b.why: Priya has gained independence and new responsibilities, and her routine now affects her sleep and exercise. The option on paid work always lowering health is wrong, because the card says work can also help health through income and purpose.
b.clue: Look for the option that links a change in roles to health without saying it always happens.

proposal.title: The move from youth to adulthood
card: The move from youth to adulthood is a time of change in roles. Young people often gain more independence and take on more responsibility for their own choices.
Common changes include finishing school, starting study or paid work, moving out of the family home and forming long-term relationships.
These changes can affect health. Paid work can bring income for things like healthy food and housing, and a sense of purpose. It can also bring stress, long hours or less time for sleep and exercise.
The effect depends on the person and their situation. Support from family, friends and the community can help a person manage the change.
proposal.remember: Becoming an adult brings new roles and responsibilities, and these can help or harm health.

a.q: Tom starts full-time work after Year 12. Which is a way this change can help his health?
opts: His income can pay for healthy food and a safe home
His long shifts can cut down his time for exercise
His new boss can add to the stress in his day
His early starts can leave him less time to sleep
a.why: Income from work can pay for things that support health, such as healthy food and housing. The other three are real effects of work, but they are risks that can harm health, not benefits.
a.clue: Work brings benefits as well as risks.

b.q: Priya, 19, has moved out of home in Geelong to start a full-time job. She pays her own rent and has little time for sleep or exercise. Which choice would most likely help her manage the move?
opts: Her friends help her plan and share cheap, healthy meals
She picks up extra shifts so she can pay her rent sooner
She stays up late most nights to finish her housework
She skips some meals so she has more money for her rent
b.why: Support from friends can help a person manage the change to adult roles, and sharing healthy meals eases her load. Extra shifts may bring more income, but they add long hours and cut her sleep and exercise even further.
b.clue: What does the card say can help a person manage the change?

a.best: His income can pay for healthy food and a safe home

b.best: Her friends help her plan and share cheap, healthy meals
